title: The $R$-Process Alliance: The $R$-Process Enhancement of Stars from Chemodynamically Tagged Groups in the Milky Way Halo
comment: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: As part of the ongoing work of the $R$-Process Alliance (RPA), detailed abundance measurements of 29 heavy elements in three metal-poor stars, 2MASS J14592981$-$3852558, 2MASS J19445483$-$4039459, and 2MASS J15211026$-$0607566, are presented based on an analysis of high-resolution ($R\sim 80,000$), high signal-to-noise ``portrait'' spectra from the Magellan Inamori Kyocera Echelle (MIKE) spectrograph on the Magellan-Clay Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory. The selected targets were identified as $r$-process-enhanced metal-poor stars in previous RPA snapshot analyses. They have also been linked to possible chemodynamically tagged groups, indicating that the stars may have formed in dwarf galaxies that were later accreted into the Milky Way halo. These stars have also been tentatively linked to the Thamnos structure. The detailed chemical abundances in this work confirm that 2MASS J14592981$-$3852558 and J15211026$-$0607566 are $r$-II stars, while 2MASS J19445483$-$4039459 is found to lie just below the threshold for $r$-I status. The $r$-II stars show signs of slight enhancement in fission fragments compared to 2MASS J19445483$-$4039459. Based on radioactive age dating with Th, the $r$-process material in the two $r$-II stars is found to be old (with ages $>10$ Gyr); neither star shows signs of an actinide boost. The varying elemental compositions suggest that these stars likely did not originate in the same environment, though each could be consistent with originating in the Thamnos progenitor.

AI.tldr: This paper presents detailed heavy-element abundance measurements of three metal-poor stars using high-resolution MIKE spectra, classifying two as r-II stars and one as r-I, with old ages (>10 Gyr) and no actinide boost, suggesting different formation environments potentially linked to the Thamnos structure.
AI.motivation: To characterize the detailed chemical abundances of r-process-enhanced metal-poor stars that may have originated in accreted dwarf galaxies, and to investigate their potential chemodynamical links to structures like Thamnos.
AI.method: High-resolution (R~80,000) MIKE spectroscopy on the Magellan-Clay Telescope; detailed abundance analysis of 29 heavy elements; radioactive age dating using Th.
AI.result: Two stars (J1459 and J1521) are confirmed as r-II stars; J1944 lies just below the r-I threshold; r-II stars show slight fission fragment enhancement; all stars are old (>10 Gyr) with no actinide boost.
AI.conclusion: The three stars likely did not originate in the same formation environment, though each could be consistent with a Thamnos progenitor origin.

title: The Extended Plane of the Local Supercluster
summary: An update of the evidence that radio galaxies and clusters of galaxies are more common than average near the plane of the de Vaucouleurs Local Supercluster shows that in the distance range 100 to 200Mpc objects whose positions are correlated with the plane of the Local Supercluster include galaxies that are exceptionally luminous at two microns, radio galaxies, and clusters of galaxies. There can be little doubt about this property of cosmic structure. I also argue for detection of this correlation for the galaxies at 400Mpc distance that are exceptionally luminous at two microns. It will be interesting to learn whether these results are expected in the standard cosmology.

AI.tldr: Radio galaxies and galaxy clusters are more common near the plane of the de Vaucouleurs Local Supercluster in the 100–200 Mpc range, with tentative evidence extending to 400 Mpc for 2μm-luminous galaxies, posing questions for standard cosmology.
AI.motivation: To update and verify the evidence that radio galaxies and galaxy clusters preferentially align with the plane of the Local Supercluster, and to test whether such large-scale structure correlations are consistent with standard cosmological predictions.
AI.method: Statistical analysis of the spatial distribution of radio galaxies, galaxy clusters, and 2μm-luminous galaxies relative to the plane of the de Vaucouleurs Local Supercluster across distance ranges of 100–200 Mpc and up to 400 Mpc.
AI.result: Objects correlated with the Local Supercluster plane in the 100–200 Mpc range include: exceptionally 2μm-luminous galaxies, radio galaxies, and clusters of galaxies. Preliminary evidence also suggests a similar correlation for 2μm-luminous galaxies at ~400 Mpc.
AI.conclusion: The alignment of these objects with the Local Supercluster plane is a robust property of cosmic structure, but its consistency with standard cosmology remains an open question requiring further investigation.

title: The applicability of the JAGB method for measuring the distance of galaxies subject to different metal enrichment rates
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The JAGB method has been proposed in recent years as a possible distance indicator for galaxies in the Local Group and beyond. However, the nature of the stars populating the J region, and the conditions required for the direct application of this method, still need to be clarified. We investigate the robustness of the JAGB method through a detailed theoretical analysis of the stars populating the J region of the (J-Ks, J) diagram. The main goal is to identify the properties of the corresponding J luminosity function (JLF) that are minimally affected by the previous evolutionary history of the host galaxy, particularly its metal enrichment history. We use a population synthesis approach based on AGB stellar evolution models coupled consistently with dust formation in the stellar wind. Synthetic stellar distributions in the (J-Ks, J) diagram and the related JLFs are calculated for different assumptions on the metallicity evolution of the interstellar medium, in order to study how the JLF depends on the efficiency of metal enrichment. We find that the JAGB population is dominated by stars formed between about 1 and 6 Gyr ago, while stars formed outside this interval contribute only marginally to the JAGB region. The shape of the JLF strongly depends on the metal enrichment history, and the position of the J-band peak varies by more than 0.3 mag among the different cases explored. Conversely, the mean J-band magnitude, MavJ, is much less sensitive to the previous history of the galaxy and therefore represents a more reliable distance indicator. For all the cases investigated we find MavJ = -6.2 +/- 0.05 mag. We also discuss the uncertainties related to the still poorly constrained mass-loss process experienced by low-mass stars during the red giant branch phase.

AI.tldr: The JAGB method's reliability as a distance indicator is tested via population synthesis modeling, finding that while the J-band peak varies (>0.3 mag) with metallicity history, the mean J-band magnitude (MavJ = -6.2 ± 0.05 mag) is robust and a more reliable distance indicator.
AI.motivation: To clarify the nature of stars populating the J region of the JAGB method and assess its robustness as a distance indicator, particularly regarding how the host galaxy's metal enrichment history affects the J luminosity function.
AI.method: Population synthesis approach using AGB stellar evolution models with consistent dust formation in stellar winds; synthetic (J-Ks, J) diagrams and JLFs computed under different metallicity evolution assumptions to study the dependence on metal enrichment efficiency.
AI.result: JAGB population is dominated by stars formed 1–6 Gyr ago. JLF shape strongly depends on metallicity history; J-band peak varies >0.3 mag across cases. However, the mean J-band magnitude (MavJ) is stable at -6.2 ± 0.05 mag, making it a more reliable distance indicator.
AI.conclusion: The mean J-band magnitude is a robust distance indicator despite metallicity variations, but uncertainties remain regarding poorly constrained mass-loss processes during the red giant branch phase.

title: Spectroscopic Bolometric Corrections and Empirical Zero-point Constants of \textit{Gaia} Magnitudes, $G$, $G_{\rm BP}$, and $G_{\rm RP}$, from \textit{Gaia} XP Spectra
comment: Accepted for publication in Physics and Astronomy Reports. 25 pages, 8 figures, and 9 tables
summary: The International Astronomical Union 2015 Resolution B2 (IAU2015GARB2) has resolved the long-standing problem of zero-point constants for the absolute and apparent bolometric magnitude scales and opened a new window in fundamental astrophysics. The empirical zero-point constants of the bolometric corrections, $C_2(ξ)$, and the absolute/apparent magnitudes, $C_ξ/c_ξ$, for the {\it Gaia} passbands were obtained from 88 {\it Gaia} XP spectra, and absolute bolometric/filtered magnitudes. The individual zero-point constants $\langle C_{\rm 2}\rangle$ of the bolometric corrections ($BC_ξ$) for each star revealed weighted averages of $\langle C_{\rm 2}(G)\rangle=0.8677\pm0.0109$ mag, $\langle C_{\rm 2}(G_{\rm BP})\rangle=1.0449\pm0.0116$ mag, and $\langle C_{\rm 2}(G_{\rm RP})\rangle=2.0510\pm0.0087$ mag. Furthermore, $C_{\rm Bol}=71.197425...$ mag and $c_{\rm Bol} =-18.997351...$mag announced by IAU2015GARB2, and using the definition of $C_{\rm 2}=C_{\rm Bol}-C_ξ=c_{\rm Bol}-c_ξ$, where the subscript $2$ indicate the wavelength ranges of two in which one is for bolometric and the other for one of the three filters, the zero-point constants of magnitudes for {\it Gaia} filters as $C_{\rm G}=70.1525\pm0.0109$ mag and $c_{\rm G}=-19.8651\pm0.0105$ mag, $C_{\rm G_{\rm BP}}=70.1525\pm0.0116$ mag and $c_{\rm G_{\rm BP}}=-20.0423\pm0.0116$ mag, and $C_{\rm G_{\rm RP}}=69.1464\pm0.0087$ mag and $c_{\rm G_{\rm RP}}=-21.0484\pm0.0087$ mag, if $L_ξ$ and $f_ξ$ are in SI units in case no extinctions. Lastly, spectroscopic $BC$s for {\it Gaia} magnitudes of 88 stars and the spectroscopic $BC-T_{\rm eff}$ relation for each {\it Gaia} filter are presented.

AI.tldr: This paper derives empirical zero-point constants for Gaia bolometric corrections and magnitude scales using 88 Gaia XP spectra, confirming IAU2015 Resolution B2 constants and presenting spectroscopic BCs and BC-Teff relations for Gaia filters.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing problem of zero-point constants for absolute and apparent bolometric magnitude scales opened by IAU2015 Resolution B2, and to obtain empirical constants specifically for Gaia passbands.
AI.method: Empirical zero-point constants C₂(ξ) and Cξ/cξ were obtained from 88 Gaia XP spectra along with absolute bolometric/filtered magnitudes. Constants were derived using the relationship C₂ = C_Bol − C_ξ = c_Bol − c_ξ, referencing IAU2015GARB2 values.
AI.result: Weighted averages: ⟨C₂(G)⟩=0.8677±0.0109 mag, ⟨C₂(GBP)⟩=1.0449±0.0116 mag, ⟨C₂(GRP)⟩=2.0510±0.0087 mag. Derived Gaia filter zero-points: CG=70.1525±0.0109 mag, CGBP=70.1525±0.0116 mag, CGRP=69.1464±0.0087 mag; cG=−19.8651±0.0105 mag, cGBP=−20.0423±0.0116 mag, cGRP=−21.0484±0.0087 mag (SI units, no extinction).
AI.conclusion: The empirical constants validate the IAU2015GARB2 framework for Gaia filters. Spectroscopic BCs for 88 stars and BC-Teff relations for each Gaia filter are provided, enabling precise bolometric corrections for Gaia photometry.

title: Variable stars in the field of the Galactic globular cluster M71
comment: 16 pages, 15 figures, 5 Tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: M71 is a nearby, metal-rich globular cluster at low Galactic latitude, where field contamination and spatially variable extinction complicate colour-magnitude diagrams (CMDs) and the identification of cluster member variable stars. Our aims are (i) to construct a homogeneous census of variable stars in M71 by refining their periods and classifications and identifying new candidates, and (ii) to derive a decontaminated, differentially dereddened CMD to constrain its physical properties. We obtained Johnson-Kron-Cousins $VI$ time-series CCD photometry and reduced it using difference image analysis. Cluster membership was established from \textit{Gaia}~DR3 proper motions, and a differential-reddening correction was applied across the field of view. The resulting CMD, cleaned of field stars, was compared with tailored isochrones to estimate age ($12.9^{+0.9}_{-0.8}$ Gyr), metallicity ([Fe/H] =$-0.88^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$), mean reddening ($E(B-V)$ = $0.21 \pm 0.02$), and distance modulus ($(m-M)_{0}$ = $13.01 \pm 0.06$). Variable stars were identified using two complementary approaches: a periodogram-free string-length scan refined with phase dispersion minimisation, and a robust inter-site screening based on median statistics combined with a generalised Lomb-Scargle significance criterion. We identified 21 variable stars not previously reported in the Catalog of Variable Stars in Globular Clusters and provided their periods, amplitudes, classifications, membership status, and light curves. This combined strategy yields a consistent picture of M71, expanding its known variable-star population and confirming parameters typical of metal-rich Galactic disk globular clusters.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive census of variable stars in the metal-rich globular cluster M71, identifying 21 new variable stars using time-series VI photometry with difference image analysis, Gaia DR3 proper motions for membership, and differential reddening correction. The cleaned CMD yields cluster parameters: age 12.9 Gyr, [Fe/H] = -0.88, E(B-V) = 0.21, and distance modulus 13.01.
AI.motivation: To construct a homogeneous variable-star census in M71 by refining known classifications and identifying new candidates, and to derive a decontaminated, differentially dereddened CMD to constrain the cluster's physical properties—motivated by challenges from field contamination and spatially variable extinction at low Galactic latitude.
AI.method: Johnson-Kron-Cousins VI time-series CCD photometry reduced via difference image analysis; Gaia DR3 proper motions for cluster membership; differential reddening correction; isochrone fitting for cluster parameters; variable star identification via periodogram-free string-length scan refined with phase dispersion minimization and a robust inter-site screening using median statistics combined with a generalized Lomb-Scargle significance criterion.
AI.result: 21 new variable stars identified; cluster parameters: age 12.9^{+0.9}_{-0.8} Gyr, [Fe/H] = -0.88^{+0.13}_{-0.15}, E(B-V) = 0.21 ± 0.02, (m-M)_0 = 13.01 ± 0.06.
AI.conclusion: The combined strategy yields a consistent picture of M71, expanding its known variable-star population and confirming parameters typical of metal-rich Galactic disk globular clusters.

title: Observational Signatures and Constraints on the Intermediate Neutron-Capture Process. The Case of the CEMP star TYC 6044-714-1 (RAVE J094921.8-161722)
summary: Observational abundances of CEMP stars with patterns in between those produced by the rapid and slow nucleosynthesis processes (CEMP-rs stars) are currently invoked as evidence of synthesis via the intermediate process in the early AGB evolutionary phase of metal-poor low mass stars. Nevertheless, discriminating between r+s- and i-process hypotheses requires high-precision abundances obtained through advanced spectral modelling techniques. Theoretical models of the i-process have become more robust, incorporating refined stellar modelling and nuclear reaction physics, providing ranges of probable elemental abundances and isotopic ratios predictions to be confronted with observational determinations. We performed a new analysis of a high resolution and high S/N UVES spectrum of TYC 6044-714-1. We derived accurate effective temperature and highly precise atmospheric parameters, element abundances, and isotopic ratios using state-of-the-art 1D non-LTE and 3D non-LTE spectral line modelling. Using the latest AGB nucleosynthesis models, we assessed the possibility of the i-process to act aside the s-process. We find that TYC~6044-714-1 was likely born as a normal in-situ halo star about 13 Gyr ago, pre-enriched by the r-process through a standard Galactic chemical-evolution pathway. The s+r model provides the best overall reproduction of the observed heavy-element abundance pattern and Ba isotopic ratios, yielding excellent agreement across all three s-process peaks. While i+s+r models with increasing overshooting efficiency improve the fit for specific elements, they do not consistently reproduce the full abundance pattern. The i+s+r models require extreme and physically implausible conditions, and predict s-process Ba fractions inconsistent with those inferred from isotopic ratios of the 4934 Å resonance line. We conclude that the pure s+r scenario is the most plausible explanation.

AI.tldr: A high-precision spectroscopic analysis of the star TYC 6044-714-1 shows its heavy-element abundance pattern is best explained by a pure s+r (slow+rapid) nucleosynthesis process, ruling out the intermediate (i-process) scenario that requires physically implausible conditions.
AI.motivation: To discriminate between the r+s- and i-process hypotheses for CEMP-rs stars by performing a state-of-the-art spectral analysis of TYC 6044-714-1, testing whether the i-process is required to explain its observed abundances.
AI.method: High-resolution, high-S/N UVES spectroscopy of TYC 6044-714-1; 1D non-LTE and 3D non-LTE spectral modelling to derive atmospheric parameters, elemental abundances, and Ba isotopic ratios; comparison with AGB nucleosynthesis models (s+r vs. i+s+r scenarios with varying overshooting efficiency).
AI.result: The s+r model best reproduces the observed heavy-element abundance pattern and Ba isotopic ratios across all three s-process peaks. i+s+r models improve fits for specific elements but require extreme, physically implausible conditions and predict s-process Ba fractions inconsistent with isotopic constraints from the 4934 Å line.
AI.conclusion: The pure s+r scenario is the most plausible explanation for TYC 6044-714-1, casting doubt on the necessity of invoking the i-process for this CEMP-rs star.

title: The Internal Nebular Attenuation Curve of Three-Dimensional Turbulent HII regions
summary: The internal dust attenuation of the Hii region reduces the observed emission-line fluxes. Turbulent density fields within each Hii region change the degree of the line-of-the-sight obscuration of the emission-line fluxes. In this paper, we implement the dust Monte-Carlo radiative transfer in the latest M3D code, creating the emission-line maps attenuated by the internal turbulent dust obscuration with the varying Mach numbers. The internal density and temperature fluctuations of Hii regions make the radiative transfer of hydrogen lines neither Case A nor Case B conditions, resulting in the global Hα to H\b{eta} ratio of approximately 3.02-3.03, differing from the widely-used value of 2.86. This deviation from Case B is because the temperature of these Hii regions is cooler than 10,000 K. We further derive the internal nebular attenuation curve from the attenuated Hydrogen lines, finding that the clumpy structures within Hii regions do not change the slope of the internal attenuation curve. This is because the heavy dust obscuration of dense clumps is canceled out by the high in-situ production of emission-line intensities.

AI.tldr: This paper implements dust Monte-Carlo radiative transfer in the M3D code to study how turbulent density fields in Hii regions affect emission-line fluxes and internal dust attenuation, finding that the Hα/Hβ ratio deviates from the standard Case B value (3.02-3.03 vs. 2.86) due to cooler temperatures, and that clumpy structures do not alter the slope of the internal attenuation curve.
AI.motivation: To understand how internal dust attenuation and turbulent density fields within Hii regions affect observed emission-line fluxes, and to determine whether clumpy structures influence the internal attenuation curve.
AI.method: Implementing dust Monte-Carlo radiative transfer in the M3D code to create emission-line maps attenuated by internal turbulent dust obscuration across varying Mach numbers.
AI.result: The global Hα/Hβ ratio is approximately 3.02-3.03 rather than the standard 2.86, and clumpy structures do not change the slope of the internal attenuation curve.
AI.conclusion: The deviation from Case B recombination arises because Hii regions are cooler than 10,000 K, and the cancellation between heavy dust obscuration of dense clumps and high in-situ emission-line production explains the unchanged attenuation curve slope.

title: Chemical signatures of planetary systems in their host stars. Near-infrared spectroscopy of four planet-hosting wide binaries
comment: 19 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: An important open question in exoplanet studies is whether planets leave detectable chemical fingerprints on their host stars. While several studies have suggested possible planetary chemical signatures in planet-hosting stars, their origin remains debated because of stellar birth conditions and evolutionary effects. Wide binaries, whose components share a common formation environment, provide an ideal testbed for identifying planetary signatures. Such signatures are often characterized by differential abundance trends with condensation temperature (Tc), which traces the partitioning between gaseous and rocky planetary material. We investigate whether these trends are associated with planetary architectures in wide binaries. We obtained high-resolution NIR spectra of four planet-hosting wide binaries. We measured abundances for both components and analyzed differential abundances in each system. We also compiled literature measurements for planet-hosting and non-hosting wide binaries and compared their Tc trends. WASP-160 A/B and WASP-127/TYC 4916-897-1 exhibit significant abundance trends with Tc, while HD 20782/HD 20781 shows a weaker correlation and K2-54/K2-54 B is consistent with a flat relation. The trends are diverse, including both volatile- and refractory-enhanced patterns in planet-hosting stars. Literature comparisons indicate that extreme Tc slopes may occur more frequently among planet-hosting wide binaries, particularly at large separations, although the statistics remain limited by sample size and definition. Our results indicate that chemical signatures in planet-hosting wide binaries are not universal but vary across systems. While planetary architectures may be associated with some host-star abundance patterns, multiple processes are likely to contribute. Larger samples are essential for disentangling planetary signatures from stellar and binary effects.

AI.tldr: This study investigates whether planets leave chemical fingerprints on their host stars by analyzing abundance trends with condensation temperature (Tc) in four planet-hosting wide binaries. Results show diverse Tc trends—some significant, some weak, some flat—suggesting planetary chemical signatures are not universal and likely arise from multiple processes, with extreme Tc slopes possibly more frequent in planet-hosting wide binaries at large separations.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether planets imprint detectable chemical signatures on their host stars, using wide binaries (which share common formation environments) to isolate planetary effects from stellar birth conditions and evolutionary effects.
AI.method: High-resolution NIR spectroscopy of four planet-hosting wide binaries (WASP-160 A/B, WASP-127/TYC 4916-897-1, HD 20782/HD 20781, K2-54/K2-54 B) to measure elemental abundances and differential abundance trends with condensation temperature (Tc), supplemented by literature compilation of planet-hosting and non-hosting wide binaries.
AI.result: WASP-160 A/B and WASP-127/TYC 4916-897-1 show significant Tc trends; HD 20782/HD 20781 shows a weaker correlation; K2-54/K2-54 B shows a flat relation. Trends include both volatile- and refractory-enhanced patterns. Literature suggests extreme Tc slopes may be more frequent in planet-hosting wide binaries at large separations, but statistics are limited.
AI.conclusion: Chemical signatures in planet-hosting wide binaries are not universal and vary across systems. While planetary architectures may contribute to some abundance patterns, multiple processes are likely involved; larger samples are needed to disentangle planetary signatures from stellar and binary effects.

title: Exploring the stellar streams and satellites around the giant low surface brightness galaxy Malin 1
summary: Context. Giant Low Surface Brightness galaxies, such as Malin 1, host extended discs exceeding 100 kpc. Their formation and evolution remain debated, with interactions with satellite galaxies and accretion streams proposed as key contributors. Malin 1 hosts satellites and exhibits two giant stellar streams, likely the result of past interactions. Aims. We investigate the orbital dynamics of Malin 1's satellites and their possible connections with observed stellar streams, testing their nature with different formation scenarios. Methods. We constructed gravitational potentials using optical and HI data, including stellar, gaseous, and dark matter components, and explored a wide parameter space while testing NFW and ISO halo profiles. Results. Some scenarios produced bound solutions. The ISO halo model ($M_{\text{Virial}} \approx 2.6 \times 10^{12}~M_{\odot}$) favours bound satellite orbits more than the NFW model ($M_{\text{Virial}} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{12}~M_{\odot}$). Giant stellar streams could be substructures of some satellite galaxies along their leading and trailing trajectories. The most distant Malin 1 satellite could have reached pericenter $\sim 1.6$ Gyr ago, while closer companions interacted as early as $\sim 100$ Myr ago. At the same time, one close companion displays both leading and trailing arms in radial and polar orbits. Furthermore, we also identify some unbound solutions linking satellites with streams. Conclusions. Satellites and stream alignment indicate that past interactions shaped Malin 1's morphology. Our modelling constrains progenitors and orbital histories, providing insights into the dynamical evolution of gLSBGs. Findings are consistent with recent studies using Malin 1 kinematic data.

AI.tldr: This study models the gravitational potential of Malin 1 using optical, HI, and dark matter data, finding that satellite orbits (especially under an ISO halo) can explain observed giant stellar streams through past interactions, with bound and unbound solutions linking satellites to stream formation over timescales from ~100 Myr to ~1.6 Gyr.
AI.motivation: To investigate the orbital dynamics of Malin 1's satellites and their possible connections with observed stellar streams, testing their nature with different formation scenarios.
AI.method: Constructed gravitational potentials using optical and HI data, including stellar, gaseous, and dark matter components, explored a wide parameter space testing NFW and ISO halo profiles.
AI.result: ISO halo model (M_Virial ~ 2.6×10^12 M⊙) favors bound satellite orbits more than NFW model (M_Virial ~ 1.4×10^12 M⊙). Giant stellar streams could be substructures of satellite galaxies along leading/trailing trajectories. Most distant satellite pericenter ~1.6 Gyr ago, closer companions ~100 Myr ago. One close companion shows leading/trailing arms in radial and polar orbits. Some unbound solutions also identified.
AI.conclusion: Satellites and stream alignment indicate past interactions shaped Malin 1's morphology. Modeling constrains progenitors and orbital histories, providing insights into gLSBG dynamical evolution, consistent with recent kinematic studies.

title: Continuous mass ablation of planets engulfed in stellar envelopes
comment: Submitted to A&A. Animated figures are available via https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZvLCitllq5s5MXv1hH1TnzruyMMslkZ9&si=KW-R2q9AHpAuUZuc
summary: Most stars host short-period planets that are expected to be engulfed during post-main-sequence expansion. The dissolution of engulfed planets has been proposed as a possible mechanism for producing stars enriched in lithium and refractory elements. We perform three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of a Jupiter-like planet engulfed within a stellar envelope using the Seven-League Hydro code. Unlike previous studies that represent the planet as a point mass or rigid sphere, we adopt a wind-tunnel setup that resolves the planet's gaseous structure. We find that a continuous mass-ablation process operates during planetary engulfment, contrary to the common assumption that destruction occurs at a specific depth due to ram pressure, tidal forces, or thermal evaporation. The ablation rate scales nearly linearly with the wind momentum flux and is largely insensitive to the Mach number, consistent with an analytical model based on Kelvin-Helmholtz instability developing at the planetary surface. We define efficiency coefficients for drag and ablation, finding pressure-drag coefficients of 0.44-0.56 and smaller ablation efficiencies of 0.054-0.11. Applying these coefficients to a numerically integrated inspiral through a stellar profile, we find that continuous ablation could lead to complete dissolution of the planet within the convective envelope, producing observable lithium enrichment at the stellar surface. Our results provide prescriptions for drag and mass loss that enable large parameter-space studies of planetary engulfment and suggest that chemical enrichment may occur over a broader range of stellar parameters than previously thought.

AI.tldr: Using 3D hydrodynamical simulations with a resolved gaseous planet structure, this paper shows that Jupiter-like planets undergo continuous mass ablation during stellar engulfment (rather than sudden destruction), with ablation rates scaling linearly with wind momentum flux, leading to potential observable lithium enrichment at stellar surfaces.
AI.motivation: To understand the mechanism of planetary engulfment during post-main-sequence stellar expansion, a process expected for most short-period planets, and to test whether dissolved planets can explain observed stellar enrichment in lithium and refractory elements.
AI.method: Three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations using the Seven-League Hydro code with a wind-tunnel setup that resolves the planet's gaseous structure (unlike previous point-mass or rigid-sphere treatments). Analytical modeling based on Kelvin-Helmholtz instability at the planetary surface. Numerical integration of inspiral through a stellar profile with defined drag and ablation efficiency coefficients.
AI.result: Continuous mass ablation operates during engulfment (not sudden destruction). Ablation rate scales nearly linearly with wind momentum flux and is largely Mach-number-insensitive. Pressure-drag coefficients are 0.44-0.56; ablation efficiencies are 0.054-0.11. Continuous ablation can lead to complete dissolution within the convective envelope and observable lithium enrichment.
AI.conclusion: Planetary engulfment produces chemical enrichment over a broader range of stellar parameters than previously thought, and the provided drag and mass-loss prescriptions enable large-scale parameter-space studies of this process.

title: Metal Enrichment by the First Stars Exploding at the Lower Energy Limit of Pair-Instability Supernovae
summary: The first generation of stars, Population III (Pop III), is believed to be massive, with some potentially having masses in the range 140 M$_\odot$ to 270 M$_\odot$ and capable of exploding as a pair-instability supernova (PISN). Such events release large amounts of energy and produce substantial quantities of metals, suggesting that they should leave characteristic signatures in the abundance patterns of extremely metal-poor (EMP) stars observed in the local Universe. No clear imprint of PISNe is seen in the local EMP star population, implying either that these events were rare or that stars forming from PISN-enriched gas had metallicities too high to find them in the EMP population. Previous work explored the latter possibility by investigating the enrichment by PISNe with masses and explosion energies at the upper end of the theoretical range (270 M$_\odot$, $10^{53}$ erg). Here, we complement that work at the opposite extreme: Pop III stars at the lower mass (140 M$_\odot$) and explosion energy ($5\cdot 10^{51}$ erg) limit. Using a cosmological hydrodynamic simulation, we self-consistently track the formation of Pop III stars, their radiative and mechanical feedback, and the subsequent formation of second-generation stars in metal-enriched gas. We find that all second-generation stars are exclusively internally enriched by their progenitor within the same halo, thereby imprinting the abundance pattern of a single first-generation star. The median [Fe/H] abundance of second-generation stars is ~ -5.5 which is 2.9 dex smaller than in the high-energy PISN case. Our results demonstrate that if Pop III PISNe were common, we would expect to find stars with the characteristic odd-even abundance pattern produced by PISNe within the observed EMP population. Their absence in observations therefore strongly disfavours PISNe as the dominant channel of early metal enrichment.

AI.tldr: This study simulates low-mass (140 M☉) pair-instability supernovae (PISNe) from Population III stars and finds that second-generation stars form with very low metallicities ([Fe/H] ~ -5.5) and carry characteristic odd-even abundance patterns from single progenitor enrichment. The absence of such patterns in observed EMP stars strongly disfavors PISNe as a dominant early enrichment channel.
AI.motivation: To test whether low-mass (140 M☉) PISNe could explain the enrichment signatures expected in extremely metal-poor (EMP) stars, and to resolve the tension between theoretical predictions of PISN imprints and their absence in observations.
AI.method: Cosmological hydrodynamic simulation tracking Pop III star formation, radiative and mechanical feedback, and second-generation star formation in metal-enriched gas, focusing on the lower end of the PISN mass (140 M☉) and explosion energy (5×10⁵¹ erg) range.
AI.result: All second-generation stars are internally enriched by a single progenitor within the same halo, with median [Fe/H] ≈ -5.5, which is 2.9 dex lower than in high-energy PISN cases. The characteristic odd-even abundance pattern from PISNe is preserved in these stars.
AI.conclusion: If PISNe were a dominant enrichment channel, stars bearing their odd-even abundance signature should be observable in the EMP population. Their absence strongly disfavors PISNe as the primary source of early metal enrichment.

title: An investigation of magnetic energy and helicity thresholds at the onset of solar eruptions based on numerical simulations
summary: Identifying universal, topology-independent thresholds in the coronal magnetic fields at onset of solar eruptions is crucial for physics-based prediction of eruptions. To this end, we systematically analyze the evolution of magnetic energy and helicity in twelve high-fidelity 3D magnetohydrodynamic simulations where eruptions are triggered by magnetic reconnection. The simulations encompass a comprehensive parameter space, including bipolar and quadrupolar configurations, sheared arcades and pre-existing flux ropes, and various photospheric driving motions. We find that the ratio of current-carrying helicity to total relative helicity $(H_j/H_r)$ exhibits a remarkably consistent threshold of $0.38 \pm 0.04$ at eruption onset across all cases, with a coefficient of variation of only $\sim 10$\%. This threshold specifically characterizes the critical conditions at eruption onset and is largely independent of the subsequent temporal evolution, making it the most robust eruptivity indicator identified. In contrast, other normalized helicity and energy metrics show greater scatter. Crucially, we further find that $H_j/H_r$ does not necessarily achieve its peak at the eruption onset time and its post-eruption evolution diverges based on magnetic topology: it continues to increase in bipolar configurations due to tether-cutting reconnection, which transforms sheared arcade into the erupting current-carrying magnetic flux, but decreases in quadrupolar configurations as breakout reconnection peels off the erupting flux. These results highlight the helicity ratio as a promising and consistent eruptivity indicator and provide new insights into its dynamic evolution due to different reconnections.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes 12 MHD simulations of solar eruptions and finds that the ratio of current-carrying helicity to total relative helicity ($H_j/H_r$) consistently reaches $0.38 \pm 0.04$ at eruption onset across various magnetic topologies, making it the most robust eruptivity indicator identified.
AI.motivation: To identify universal, topology-independent thresholds in coronal magnetic fields at solar eruption onset for physics-based prediction of eruptions.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of magnetic energy and helicity evolution in twelve high-fidelity 3D MHD simulations covering bipolar/quadrupolar configurations, sheared arcades/pre-existing flux ropes, and various photospheric driving motions, with eruptions triggered by magnetic reconnection.
AI.result: The helicity ratio $H_j/H_r$ shows a consistent threshold of $0.38 \pm 0.04$ (coefficient of variation ~10%) at eruption onset across all cases, outperforming other normalized helicity and energy metrics. Post-eruption evolution differs by topology: increases in bipolar (tether-cutting reconnection) vs. decreases in quadrupolar (breakout reconnection) configurations.
AI.conclusion: $H_j/H_r$ is a promising and consistent eruptivity indicator for solar eruptions, though its post-eruption dynamics depend on the reconnection regime and magnetic topology.

title: Non-LTE atmosphere models of very luminous sources and their applicability to Little Red Dots, quasi-stars, and similar objects
comment: 16 pages. Submitted to A&A. Comments welcome
summary: We investigate whether atmosphere models traditionally used for massive stars with strong winds can produce synthetic spectra morphologically similar to those of Little Red Dots (LRDs). We compute atmosphere models and synthetic spectra with the code CMFGEN. The models assume a thermalized radiation field at the inner boundary, parameterized by a temperature varying between 5000 and 12000~K. We adopt a typical luminosity of 1e10 Lsun. The models are spherical, assume an expanding atmosphere, and are computed under non-LTE conditions and for several metallicities. The spectral energy distribution (SED) is different from a blackbody, with a blue optical spectrum. Broad hydrogen emission lines are produced, their wings being formed by electron scattering. The SED near the Balmer and Paschen limit is rather continuous. A Balmer break is predicted for the coolest temperature models provided the wind density is reduced. The SED and Balmer decrement of most LRDs is reproduced by the models, provided they are dust-attenuated with Av~1.9-2.7. Assuming the absorbed luminosity is re-radiated in the infrared, the energy output at these wavelengths is consistent with observational constraints. The models predict FeII, oxygen and calcium lines. OI lines at 8446 A and 1.129 um are produced mostly by Lybeta fluorescence. The strength of emission lines from metals depends on input temperature, metallicity, and details of the radiative transfer models. CMFGEN atmosphere models predict a large number of spectral properties observed in many LRDs. They struggle to simultaneously produce a genuine Balmer break and strong emission lines. Whether they are more relevant or not to explain LRDs' spectra compared to alternative models is unclear, leaving open the question of the physical conditions in LRDs.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether expanding atmosphere models (CMFGEN) used for massive stars with strong winds can reproduce the observed spectra of Little Red Dots (LRDs). Models with temperatures 5000–12000 K, luminosity 1e10 Lsun, and non-LTE conditions produce blue optical SEDs, broad hydrogen emission lines via electron scattering, and metal lines (FeII, OI, Ca). Dust attenuation (Av~1.9–2.7) reproduces most LRD SEDs. However, the models cannot simultaneously produce a genuine Balmer break and strong emission lines, leaving the nature of LRDs uncertain.
AI.motivation: To test whether atmosphere models traditionally applied to massive stars with strong winds can produce synthetic spectra that morphologically resemble those of Little Red Dots (LRDs), whose physical nature remains unknown.
AI.method: Spherical, expanding atmosphere models computed with CMFGEN under non-LTE conditions, with thermalized inner boundary temperatures 5000–12000 K, luminosity 1e10 Lsun, and varying metallicities. Spectra are compared to observed LRDs with dust attenuation applied.
AI.result: Models produce blue optical SEDs, broad hydrogen emission lines via electron scattering, and metal lines (FeII, OI, Ca). Dust attenuation with Av~1.9–2.7 reproduces most LRD SEDs. However, models cannot simultaneously produce a genuine Balmer break and strong emission lines.
AI.conclusion: CMFGEN atmosphere models predict many spectral properties of LRDs but struggle with the Balmer break vs. strong line tension. Whether these models are more relevant than alternatives remains unclear, leaving the physical conditions in LRDs an open question.

title: Starspot activity and surface differential rotation on UX Arietis
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present new Doppler images of the K0 subgiant primary component of the RS CVn-type binary UX Arietis (UX Ari), derived from time-series spectra obtained in November--December of 2017 and 2024. Observations demonstrate that some spectral lines of the K0 IV component exhibit rapid changes on timescales of 1-2 hours, which seem not to be resulting from spot activity, meanwhile other spectral lines show no such fast variations. Through an investigation, we find that the Ca I 6439 $\unicode{x212B}$ profile shows variation that follows the rotational modulation of spots. Using this line as a reference, we derive the least-squares deconvolution (LSD) profile from the selected lines of each spectrum so as to generate a more reliable Doppler image, which is consistent with the shape of the corresponding Ca I 6439 $\unicode{x212B}$ line. The Doppler images are separately reconstructed from the Ca I 6439 $\unicode{x212B}$ and the LSD profiles for each dataset, and the surface maps are in good agreement with each other. All of the surface maps show dominant starspot structure at mid-to-high latitudes with appendages extending to the equator, while their locations differ by about 0.5 in the rotational phase between 2017 and 2024. In 2017 November-December, the main starspot group appears to be spatially associated with a large flare event just half a month later. Through the cross-correlation method, we have derived a weak anti-solar differential rotation for the primary component of UX Ari, while its equator belt is well tidally locked.

AI.tldr: New Doppler images of UX Ari (K0 subgiant in RS CVn binary) from 2017 and 2024 spectra reveal rapid spectral line variations (1-2 hr), spot-modulated Ca I 6439 Å line, consistent LSD-based surface maps showing mid-to-high latitude starspots extending to equator, phase shift of ~0.5 between epochs, association of 2017 spot group with a flare, and weak anti-solar differential rotation with tidally locked equatorial belt.
AI.motivation: To study surface inhomogeneities (starspots) and differential rotation on the active K0 subgiant component of UX Ari, a classical RS CVn-type binary, using new spectroscopic observations separated by 7 years.
AI.method: Time-series spectroscopy (Nov-Dec 2017 and 2024); identification of Ca I 6439 Å as a spot-rotationally modulated line; least-squares deconvolution (LSD) to generate reliable profiles from selected lines; Doppler imaging reconstruction from both Ca I 6439 Å and LSD profiles; cross-correlation to measure differential rotation.
AI.result: Rapid (1-2 hr) spectral line variations exist in some lines but not others; Ca I 6439 Å follows rotational spot modulation; Doppler maps from Ca I 6439 Å and LSD agree; dominant mid-to-high latitude spots with equatorial extensions; spot locations shift ~0.5 in phase from 2017 to 2024; 2017 spot group linked to a flare ~0.5 month later; weak anti-solar differential rotation detected; equatorial belt is tidally locked.
AI.conclusion: UX Ari's primary exhibits stable, long-lived starspot structures with measurable differential rotation and tidal locking at the equator, and some spectral lines show rapid variations unexplained by spot activity, warranting further investigation.

title: Proximate damped Lyman-$α$ systems as tracers of quasar feedback
comment: 12 pages, 17 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: Active galactic nuclei (AGN) profoundly affect the interstellar medium of their host galaxies through intense radiation fields and powerful winds. Characterising this feedback is essential for understanding galaxy formation and evolution. Here we revisit the origin of proximate damped Lyman-$α$ absorbers (PDLAs), which trace cold gas within 3000 km/s of the quasar redshift, and interpret their kinematics and physical properties within a unified framework. We searched the SDSS DR16 database for low-ionisation metal absorption-line systems at the quasar redshift (referred to as ProxSys). This approach enables us to identify and classify different types of proximate absorbers, including so-called Ghostly systems, coronagraphic DLAs (DLA-Cor), standard DLAs, and sub-DLAs, based on the presence of strong Lyman-alpha absorption, partial covering signatures, or excited atomic transitions such as SiII*. We find that about 13% of ProxSys belong to the Ghostly or DLA-Cor classes and exhibit strong absorption from excited species. The different classes of ProxSys form a continuous sequence characterised by decreasing SiII*, CIV, and NV absorption strengths and dust content. Their velocity distributions reveal multiple kinematic components. Standard DLAs cluster within 1000km/s of the quasar systemic redshift, consistent with gas in the host galaxy, whereas Ghostly and SiII* bearing systems display broader distributions, including outflows reaching -2000 km/s and a smaller population of inflowing clouds up to +1200 km/s. Median stacked spectra confirm that Ghostly and coronagraphic systems arise in dense, compact gas partially covering the quasar emission regions. These results support a scenario in which cold, dense clouds participate in a dynamic cycle of inflow and outflow in the vicinity of quasars, consistent with chaotic cold accretion.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes SDSS DR16 data on proximate absorption systems (ProxSys) near quasars, classifying them into Ghostly, coronagraphic DLAs, standard DLAs, and sub-DLAs. About 13% are Ghostly/DLA-Cor with strong excited species absorption. They form a continuous sequence based on SiII*, CIV, NV, and dust content. Standard DLAs cluster within 1000 km/s (host galaxy gas), while Ghostly/SiII* systems show broader distributions (outflows to -2000 km/s, inflows to +1200 km/s). Results support a dynamic cycle of cold chaotic accretion inflows and outflows near quasars.
AI.motivation: To understand AGN feedback on the interstellar medium of host galaxies by characterizing the kinematics and physical properties of proximate damped Lyman-α absorbers (PDLAs) and related systems.
AI.method: Searched SDSS DR16 for low-ionization metal absorption-line systems at quasar redshift (ProxSys), classified them based on Lyman-α absorption strength, partial covering signatures, and excited transitions (SiII*), and analyzed their kinematics via velocity distributions and median stacked spectra.
AI.result: ~13% are Ghostly/DLA-Cor with strong excited absorption; classes form a continuous sequence in SiII*, CIV, NV, and dust content; standard DLAs cluster within 1000 km/s, while Ghostly/SiII* systems show outflows to -2000 km/s and inflows to +1200 km/s.
AI.conclusion: Cold, dense clouds participate in a dynamic cycle of inflow and outflow near quasars, consistent with chaotic cold accretion.

title: An eclipsing CEMP candidate discovered in a search for dwarf carbon stars in post-common envelope binaries
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables, submitted to MNRAS
summary: Dwarf carbon stars are dominated by members of the Galactic halo and are thus likely carbon-enhanced metal-poor stars. In this work, a sample of 879 bona fide dwarf carbon stars are characterized by their ground-based light curves, and p<15 d modulation is found to be significant in 31 objects (3.5%), consistent with starspots and rotation in tidally-locked, post-common envelope binaries. Among these is an unambiguous halo star that is eclipsing every 1.224 d, and where the 30% eclipse depth rules out a white dwarf occulter. Available Gaia data do not indicate any tertiary in the eclipsing system, but this remains a possibility and follow-up data are necessary to determine the evolutionary history of this first eclipsing binary among carbon-enhanced stars. Four of the variable sources exhibit clear multi-year, quasi-sinusoidal trends indicative of magnetic-activity and starspot cycles in rapidly-rotating, dynamo-rejuvenated stars. These data support a picture where carbon pollution results from wind capture prior to Roche lobe overflow, and the orbital period distribution appears to be moderately shifted to longer periods than carbon-normal, low-mass stars in similar binaries. The band-combined approach adopted in this work may be more sensitive than prior work using single-bandpass light curves, where at most 19 of 34 binary candidates published by Roulston et al. (2021) are independently confirmed here.

AI.tldr: A study of 879 dwarf carbon stars finds 3.5% show short-period modulation consistent with starspots in tidally-locked binaries, including the first eclipsing binary among carbon-enhanced stars (1.224 d period, 30% depth ruling out a white dwarf occulter), and four stars show multi-year magnetic activity cycles.
AI.motivation: Dwarf carbon stars are likely carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP) stars in the Galactic halo; understanding their binary properties and variability helps constrain the mechanisms of carbon pollution and binary evolution in metal-poor environments.
AI.method: Ground-based light curves of 879 bona fide dwarf carbon stars were analyzed using a band-combined approach to detect periodic modulation (p<15 d), and variable sources were classified by light curve morphology.
AI.result: 31 objects (3.5%) show significant p<15 d modulation; one unambiguous halo star exhibits a 1.224 d eclipsing binary with 30% depth (ruling out a white dwarf occulter); four sources show multi-year quasi-sinusoidal trends indicating magnetic cycles; the orbital period distribution is moderately shifted to longer periods than carbon-normal low-mass binaries.
AI.conclusion: The data support carbon pollution via wind capture prior to Roche lobe overflow. The band-combined approach is more sensitive than single-bandpass methods. Follow-up is needed to determine the evolutionary history of the first eclipsing binary among carbon-enhanced stars.

title: A tool of Hierarchical cOre ideNtification and Kinematic property AssIgnment (HONKAI) for Dense Cores
summary: Infrared dark clouds (IRDCs) contains cold dense gas at the earliest stage of massive star and cluster formation. In studying the IRDCs, a universal and fundamental task is to resolve their internal hierarchical structures. Various packages and algorithms were developed for this purpose, but with most of them mainly focused on certain individual steps in data processing. In this work, we build a more automatic procedure for multi-band structure measurement HONKAI (Hierarchical cOre ideNtification and Kinematic property AssIgnment), which can resolve the elemental components including cores and clumps, disentangle the velocity components in spectral data, measure their physical properties, and generate a catalogue for all the measured properties. We use {\sc honkai} for a joint study towards three IRDCs observed in 850 $μ$m dust continuum with James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) and the $^{13}CO$ $(1-0)$ data cube with the Purple Mount Observatory 14-m telescope. 193 dense cores in 16 clumps are identified. As major dynamical properties, a large amount of the cores (136 out of 193) are measured to have large virial ratio of $R_{\rm vir}>1$, but their mass-size relation is bellow the threshold for massive star formation. Meanwhile, core mass function (CMF) also exhibits a steeper slope towards high-mass end compared to more evolved core samples. These three properties in accordance suggest that although many IRDC cores are self-gravitating, only a small fraction are seemingly possible to form high-mass stars. In subsequent core evolution, some further mass assembly trend may be involved to facilitate the high-mass star formation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents HONKAI, an automatic procedure for identifying hierarchical structures (cores/clumps) in Infrared Dark Clouds (IRDCs) using multi-band data. Applied to three IRDCs with JCMT 850μm and PMO 13CO data, it identifies 193 cores in 16 clumps. Most cores have virial ratio >1 but lie below the massive star formation threshold in mass-size relation, and the CMF shows a steeper high-mass slope. This suggests only a small fraction of IRDC cores can form high-mass stars, requiring further mass assembly.
AI.motivation: To address the need for an automatic, comprehensive procedure that resolves hierarchical structures in IRDCs beyond existing fragmented tools that focus only on individual processing steps.
AI.method: Develops HONKAI (Hierarchical cOre ideNtification and Kinematic property AssIgnment), an automatic pipeline integrating multi-band structure identification, velocity component disentanglement in spectral data, physical property measurement, and catalogue generation. Applied to 850μm dust continuum (JCMT) and 13CO(1-0) data (PMO 14-m telescope) for three IRDCs.
AI.result: Identified 193 dense cores within 16 clumps. 136/193 cores have virial ratio R_vir > 1. Mass-size relation lies below the massive star formation threshold. CMF shows a steeper high-mass slope compared to evolved core samples.
AI.conclusion: Most IRDC cores are self-gravitating but only a small fraction can form high-mass stars. Further mass assembly may be needed in subsequent core evolution to facilitate high-mass star formation.

title: Effect of Solar Flares on Decayless Kink Oscillations in Nearby Coronal Loops
summary: We present a statistical study of 130 solar flares (B to X class) that lack soft X-ray quasi-periodic pulsations and show no kink oscillations of nearby coronal loops visible in SDO/AIA 171~Å~images. The aim is to investigate whether decayless kink oscillations of coronal loops respond to nearby flaring activity. Using the Fractional Anisotropy-based Video Motion Magnification technique, we detected low-amplitude decayless oscillations in all 130 loops before, during, and after each flare, confirming their ubiquitous nature. Oscillation periods are found to range from 122~s to 268~s, and the projected displacement amplitudes are 0.023--0.111~Mm. No amplitude--period correlation is found. For each event, we estimated the amplitude before, during, and after the flare. Across all flare classes, the average amplitude remains unchanged. However, in some specific cases, the oscillation amplitude may exhibit minor changes. For B-, C-, and M-class flares, the fraction of events with an amplitude change exceeding 10% is approximately 23%, 41%, and 36%, respectively. In M-class flares, such minor amplitude increases occur four times more often than decreases; in X-class flares (only six events), decreases dominate by a factor of three. The fraction of events that exhibit an increase in the amplitude of more than 20% appears to be highest when the loop centre is located at a distance of 100--120~Mm from the flare site, reaching 33% (6 out of 18 events). Overall, the amplitude of decayless kink oscillations does not undergo a major change in response to nearby flares, especially for less powerful classes, suggesting that flare-related processes such as blast waves and reconnection inflows have little effect on the energy supply to oscillating loops.

AI.tldr: A statistical study of 130 solar flares (B to X class) finds that decayless kink oscillations are ubiquitous in nearby coronal loops (detected in all cases), with periods of 122–268 s and amplitudes of 0.023–0.111 Mm. The average oscillation amplitude does not change significantly during flares, though minor amplitude changes (>10%) occur in some events (23% for B, 41% for C, 36% for M class). For M-class flares, amplitude increases are 4× more common than decreases; for X-class (6 events), decreases dominate 3:1. The largest fraction of >20% amplitude increases occurs when the loop center is 100–120 Mm from the flare site (33%). Overall, nearby flares have little effect on decayless kink oscillation amplitudes, indicating blast waves and reconnection inflows do not substantially affect the energy supply to oscillating loops.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether decayless kink oscillations of coronal loops respond to nearby flaring activity, thereby testing if flare-related processes (blast waves, reconnection inflows) affect the energy supply to oscillating loops.
AI.method: Statistical analysis of 130 solar flares (B–X class) with no soft X-ray QPPs and no visible kink oscillations. Used the Fractional Anisotropy-based Video Motion Magnification technique to detect low-amplitude decayless oscillations in SDO/AIA 171 Å images before, during, and after each flare. Measured periods (122–268 s), displacement amplitudes (0.023–0.111 Mm), and amplitude changes across flare phases per flare class. Examined fraction of events with >10% and >20% amplitude changes and the dependence on distance from flare site.
AI.result: Decayless kink oscillations detected in all 130 loops, confirming their ubiquity. No amplitude–period correlation found. Average amplitude remains unchanged across all flare classes. For B, C, M classes, 23%, 41%, 36% of events showed >10% amplitude change. M-class: increases 4× more common than decreases. X-class (6 events): decreases dominate 3:1. Highest fraction of >20% amplitude increase (33%) when loop center is 100–120 Mm from flare site. Overall, no major amplitude change in response to flares, especially for less powerful classes.
AI.conclusion: Decayless kink oscillations are ubiquitous and their amplitudes do not undergo major changes in response to nearby flares (particularly for weaker classes). This suggests that flare-related processes such as blast waves and reconnection inflows have little effect on the energy supply to oscillating loops.

title: Self-consistent dynamical modelling of the Milky Way bar with orbital frequency analysis
comment: 21 pages, 19 figures, 2 tables. Re-submitted to Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society in response to reviewer report. The code used for this work is available at https://github.com/langfzac/MW_bar_paper. Comments/corrections welcome
summary: We present an update to the frequency analysis method for measuring the properties of a galactic bar. The method involves computing the fundamental frequencies of orbits in rotating, N-body-derived potential models, classifying the stars as members of bar supporting orbits, and finding the extent of the apo-centre distribution. In this work, we apply an updated classification criterion designed to isolate the so-called "Warm" inner Lindblad resonance (ILR) orbits. These orbits have been shown to contain the looped x1 orbits, which dominate the "shoulder regions" of the bar and largely contribute to the radial extent. We apply this method to existing Gaia, APOGEE, and OGLE data of more than 200,000 stars to constrain the properties of the Milky Way bar. We find that multiple bar lengths and pattern speeds are consistent with the data to within 5 percent.

AI.tldr: This paper updates a frequency analysis method for measuring galactic bar properties, applies a new classification criterion to identify Warm ILR orbits (looped x1 orbits) in N-body simulations, and uses Gaia, APOGEE, and OGLE data of 200,000+ stars to constrain the Milky Way bar, finding multiple bar lengths and pattern speeds consistent within 5%.
AI.motivation: To improve the measurement of galactic bar properties (length, pattern speed) by updating the frequency analysis method with a new classification criterion that isolates Warm Inner Lindblad Resonance (ILR) orbits, which are important for understanding bar structure, particularly the shoulder regions and radial extent.
AI.method: The method: (1) computes fundamental frequencies of orbits in rotating N-body-derived potential models, (2) classifies stars as bar-supporting orbits using an updated criterion to isolate Warm ILR orbits (looped x1 orbits), (3) measures the apo-centre distribution extent, and (4) applies the method to combined Gaia, APOGEE, and OGLE data of >200,000 stars.
AI.result: Multiple bar lengths and pattern speeds are found to be consistent with the observational data to within 5%.
AI.conclusion: The updated frequency analysis method with the Warm ILR orbit classification successfully constrains Milky Way bar properties, though degeneracies remain, indicating that multiple dynamical configurations can fit the data equally well.

title: How plasma coupling and convective-zone depth shape the rotation of solar-mass stars
comment: 9 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Stellar rotation on the main sequence is a complex function of mass and age, displaying multiple regimes whose physical origin remains only partially understood. In particular, the connection between the diversity of observed rotation rates and the internal structure and thermodynamic properties of stellar interiors is still unclear. We investigated how the depth of the convective zones and the degree of plasma coupling, quantified through the plasma coupling parameter, relate to the observed rotation rates of solar-mass stars. We used a grid of $1 \, M_\odot$ MESA stellar models with a wide range of metallicities to identify the best-matching models for 243 main-sequence stars with measured rotation periods. We then examined correlations between their rotation rates and both the structural properties of the convective zones and the corresponding convective plasma coupling parameter. For this sample, rotation rates show only weak correlations with either the convective-zone depth or the plasma coupling parameter when considered independently. However, during the first two-thirds of the main-sequence lifetime, the correlation strengthens when both factors are considered jointly through a combined convective coupling index, indicating a moderate and statistically significant relationship. For older stars, these correlations weaken and lose significance, although the thermodynamic component becomes relatively more influential. These trends suggest that microphysical plasma properties may contribute to the regulation of angular momentum loss and may be connected to the onset of weakened magnetic braking.

AI.tldr: The study of 243 solar-mass stars shows that rotation rates correlate weakly with convective zone depth or plasma coupling alone, but a combined convective coupling index shows moderate, significant correlation during the first two-thirds of main-sequence life. For older stars, correlations weaken, though thermodynamic properties become relatively more influential, suggesting plasma properties may contribute to angular momentum loss regulation and weakened magnetic braking.
AI.motivation: To understand the connection between observed stellar rotation rate diversity and the internal structure (convective zone depth) and thermodynamic properties (plasma coupling parameter) of stellar interiors, particularly regarding the physical origin of different rotation regimes on the main sequence.
AI.method: Used a grid of 1 M☉ MESA stellar models across a wide range of metallicities to identify best-matching models for 243 main-sequence stars with measured rotation periods. Analyzed correlations between rotation rates and convective zone depth, plasma coupling parameter, and a combined convective coupling index.
AI.result: Rotation rates show only weak correlations with convective zone depth or plasma coupling parameter individually. However, a combined convective coupling index reveals a moderate, statistically significant correlation during the first two-thirds of the main-sequence lifetime. For older stars, correlations weaken and lose significance, though the thermodynamic component becomes relatively more influential.
AI.conclusion: Microphysical plasma properties may contribute to the regulation of angular momentum loss and may be connected to the onset of weakened magnetic braking, suggesting a potential physical link between internal stellar structure and observed rotation patterns.

title: Elemental Abundances in the Binary Star V505 Per
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astronomical Journal
summary: We present a detailed chemical abundance analysis of the eclipsing binary system V505 Per. High resolution spectra were analyzed using the MOOG spectrum analysis code, and we determined abundances not only for iron and lithium but also for Si, Na, Ca, Mn, and Ni, elements that have not previously been analyzed in detail for this system. Abundances were computed across 15 temperature points using model atmospheres, with stellar parameters refined by minimizing abundance trends with excitation potential. We determined effective temperatures of T_eff = 6650 +/- 50 K for the primary and T_eff = 6550 +/- 50 K for the secondary, with iron abundances of [Fe/H] = -0.10 +/- 0.06 and [Fe/H] = -0.19 +/- 0.07, respectively. Most [X/Fe] ratios are consistent with solar values, though manganese is deficient. Our analysis of the effective temperatures shows that both stars lie on the hot edge of the lithium dip, consistent with Koenigsberger et al. (2025), which may help resolve the inconsistency noted of the stars lithium abundance within the dip by Baugh et al. (2013).

AI.tldr: This paper presents a detailed chemical abundance analysis of the eclipsing binary V505 Per using the MOOG code, deriving abundances for Fe, Li, Si, Na, Ca, Mn, and Ni. The primary has T_eff = 6650 K and [Fe/H] = -0.10, while the secondary has T_eff = 6550 K and [Fe/H] = -0.19. Most [X/Fe] ratios are solar-like, but Mn is deficient. Both stars lie on the hot edge of the lithium dip, resolving a previous inconsistency in Li abundance placement.
AI.motivation: To perform a comprehensive chemical abundance analysis of V505 Per, including elements not previously analyzed in detail for this system, and to resolve inconsistencies in the lithium dip interpretation from prior work.
AI.method: High-resolution spectra were analyzed using the MOOG spectrum analysis code. Abundances were computed across 15 temperature points using model atmospheres, with stellar parameters refined by minimizing abundance trends with excitation potential.
AI.result: Effective temperatures of T_eff = 6650 ± 50 K (primary) and 6550 ± 50 K (secondary) were found, with iron abundances [Fe/H] = -0.10 ± 0.06 and -0.19 ± 0.07. Most [X/Fe] ratios are solar-like; manganese is deficient. Both stars lie on the hot edge of the lithium dip.
AI.conclusion: The results align with Koenigsberger et al. (2025) and resolve the inconsistency noted by Baugh et al. (2013) regarding the stars' lithium abundance within the dip.

title: Unveiling Hidden Lyman Alpha Emitters in the DESI DR1 Data
summary: We present an automatic method based on machine-learning convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to detect Lyman alpha emitters (LAE) hidden in the Data Release 1 spectroscopic dataset of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Those LAEs mostly have incorrect redshift estimations because the current DESI pipeline is not designed to detect and measure the redshifts of galaxies at $z>2$. To uncover those sources, we first visually inspect thousands of DESI spectra and construct a sample, consisting of both LAEs and non-LAEs, for training and testing the CNN-based model to (1) detect LAEs in DESI spectra and (2) determine their Ly$α$ redshifts. The final model yields $95.2\%$ purity and $95.9\%$ completeness for detecting LAEs. We apply this model to approximately $2\times10^{6}$ spectra of sources targeted as emission-line galaxies and detect 19,685 LAEs from $z\sim2$ to $3.5$ within 12 minutes with a single GPU, illustrating the high efficiency of this model for identifying LAEs. The detected LAEs are mostly at the bright end of the luminosity function with Ly$α$ luminosity $L_{\rm Lyα} \gtrsim 10^{43}$ erg/s. The high signal-to-noise composite spectrum of the detected LAEs further shows various spectral features, including P-Cygni profiles of metal lines and MgII emission lines, possible indicators of Lyman continuum escape fraction, revealing the rich astrophysical information in this LAE sample. Finally, this sample can be used to train and validate the pipelines for redshift determination of LAEs for the preparation of the DESI-II survey.

AI.tldr: A CNN-based method detects 19,685 Lyman alpha emitters (LAEs) from DESI DR1 spectra with 95.2% purity and 95.9% completeness, correcting redshift misestimations from the standard DESI pipeline for z>2 galaxies.
AI.motivation: The DESI pipeline cannot reliably detect or measure redshifts of galaxies at z>2, causing many LAEs to have incorrect redshift estimates. A fast, automated method is needed to uncover these hidden high-redshift sources.
AI.method: A CNN model trained on visually inspected DESI spectra (LAEs and non-LAEs) for binary classification (LAE detection) and redshift determination; applied to ~2 million emission-line galaxy spectra on a single GPU.
AI.result: 95.2% purity, 95.9% completeness; 19,685 LAEs detected at z~2–3.5 in 12 minutes on a single GPU; LAEs are bright-end (L_Lyα ≳ 10^43 erg/s); composite spectrum shows P-Cygni profiles, MgII emission.
AI.conclusion: The CNN model is highly efficient for discovering LAEs in large spectroscopic surveys and provides a rich sample for studying high-z galaxies as well as training DESI-II redshift pipelines.
